subject: Media Literacy
title: Children and Digital Media Ethics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Children and Digital Media Ethics.

hook.text: A 10-year-old watches 100 targeted ads per day on her favorite app. She can't distinguish them from content.

buildup.text: Children lack the cognitive development to recognize persuasion, manipulation, and targeted advertising.

discovery.text: Despite regulations like COPPA, platforms routinely collect children's data and serve them targeted content.

twist.text: Features designed for adult engagement — autoplay, notifications, streaks — are addictive by design and used on children.

climax.text: Designing addictive platforms for users who can't consent or understand the manipulation is a fundamental ethical failure.

punchline.text: If adults can't resist the design, expecting children to is absurd.

quiz.question: Why are children especially vulnerable to digital platform manipulation?
options: They lack cognitive development to recognize persuasion and targeted advertising
